Fast approximation of the skew-normal quantile function

Source: R/skew-normal.R
qsnorm_fast.Rd

A fast approximation of skew-normal quantiles, from the INLA GMRFLib C source and originally by Thomas Luu (see the references). It needs no iterative inversion, but it is only approximate: use qsnorm() for accurate quantiles.

Usage

qsnorm_fast(p, xi = 0, omega = 1, alpha = 0)

Arguments

p

Vector of probabilities.

xi

Location parameter.

omega

Scale parameter, positive.

alpha

Shape parameter.

Value

A numeric vector of approximate quantiles. xi, omega and alpha shorter than p are recycled to its length. p of 0 and 1 give -Inf and Inf.

Details

The domain is split into tail regions, handled through the Lambert W function, and a central region, handled by a fifth-order Taylor expansion of the inverse error function about a well-chosen expansion point. Negative alpha is handled by the symmetry \(Q(u; -\alpha) = -Q(1 - u; \alpha)\). qsnorm() uses it only as the start of Newton's method.

The errors below are in units of omega, for a tail probability (p or 1 - p), and were measured for alpha in \([-30, 30]\). The result is exact for alpha = 0. For alpha of \(\pm 1\), where the quantile has a closed form, it is exact except far in the heavy tail, where 1 - p or sqrt(p) rounds: the error is about 2e-8 at a tail probability of 1e-9, 2e-3 at 1e-14 and 0.1 at 1e-16. For other alpha, the error against qsnorm() is at most about 7e-3 for p in \([0.01, 0.99]\). It is largest for a tail probability near 1e-3 (about 0.085) and smaller further out: 0.02 to 0.04 from 1e-15 to 1e-8, and up to 0.06 below 1e-15, where 1 - p rounds. The exception is the light tail (the lower tail when alpha > 0, the upper tail when alpha < 0) for alpha within about 0.015 of \(\pm 2.18\), where the fifth-order coefficient of the expansion is 0. There the error grows further out: about 0.36 at a tail probability of 1e-9, 1.1 at 1e-13 and 2.1 at 1e-16. For most alpha < 0, a p below about 1e-16 gives -Inf, and for most alpha > 0, a p within about 1e-16 of 1 gives Inf.

References

Luu, T. (2016). Fast and accurate parallel computation of quantile functions for random number generation (Doctoral thesis). UCL (University College London). https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/1482128/

See also

qsnorm() for accurate quantiles.

Examples

qsnorm_fast(c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
#> [1] -1.959964  0.000000  1.959964
qsnorm_fast(c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), xi = 2, omega = 0.5, alpha = 1)
#> [1] 1.498880 2.272476 3.119482

# The error of the approximation, in units of omega
p <- c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)
qsnorm_fast(p, alpha = 3) - qsnorm(p, alpha = 3)
#> [1] 1.231115e-05 2.147594e-03 3.810285e-13
